question: How do two agents — a planner and a worker — follow one CommHub MCP task protocol to reliably complete the dispatch, execution, reporting and verification loop, and how is a manual node (no MCP runtime) driven through the same lifecycle by hand?
trigger: The user asks to dispatch a task, take a task, verify work, or debug a stalled task
A new session's agent needs to connect to the commhub / agent-network MCP
Protocol failures such as alias_not_found, a task stopped in acked, or report_completion having no effect
A node has no agent runtime behind it (hub runtime = manual) and someone must consume its work by hand
A dispatched task sits in delivered and nobody seems to have picked it up
decision: Call the MCP tools according to the role flows and state machine defined in SKILL.md
When a parameter mismatch stalls the state, repair it per Gotchas (cancel/retry, or add the correct completion)
Judge cross-machine results from the hub task row only — never read the other side's directory
For a manual node, drive the protocol with scripts/anet_manual_node.sh and read the task row, never the session status, to decide whether work started
evidence: CommHub source tree docs-site/docs/api/mcp-tools.md — tool signatures and side effects
CommHub source tree server/src/tools.ts — the state machine's exact-match logic
Postmortems and verification of the cross-machine two-agent loop (exact task-body matching, ack/working/completion order)
references/manual-node.md — the manual-node lifecycle, its token rules, and the online-vs-working diagnosis
success_measure: The planner dispatches per the hard rules and the worker acks, reports working, and sends exactly one completion per task, so every task flips to replied on the hub and verification is read-only via get_task; a manual node's task also reaches replied, driven by the bundled script
outcome: Two agents complete a verifiable task loop under one protocol, and a manual node is driven through the same lifecycle without an agent behind it
input_types: manual node hub url and node alias
output_artifacts: manual node heartbeat and status files

examples.invocation: /agent-network-skill split this round's work and dispatch it to <worker-alias>
examples.description: The planner dispatches per the hard rules: self-contained body, ttl 86400, "do it in your working directory"

examples.invocation: /agent-network-skill take a task and report per protocol (worker side)
examples.description: The worker consumes in order: register, ack, working with the verbatim body, exactly one completion per task

examples.invocation: /agent-network-skill the manual node got a task but nothing started, check it
examples.description: The operator runs scripts/anet_manual_node.sh check and reads the per-task verdict (delivered = never acked, acked-by-someone-else = claimed under us, running = in progress, left behind = reassigned away)

examples.invocation: /agent-network-skill the manual node was given two tasks
examples.description: The operator runs check: a node has one session slot, so the second task waits its turn; the script refuses to start it in parallel

permissions_systems: Read the hub token from an environment variable or local config
Read and write the git repository of the project that mounted this skill
Run scripts/anet_manual_node.sh on the machine that owns the manual node (it writes a node config and heartbeat files there)

required_capabilities: Read the hub token from an environment variable or local config
Call the MCP tools as specified in SKILL.md
bash plus node (or bun) on PATH to run scripts/anet_manual_node.sh
readiness_checks: The MCP tool set is visible (connected)
The token exists and is the right kind (planner: utok/atok; worker: ntok)
The worker alias already has a session row on the hub
For a manual node: the node config exists and holds a node token bound to that alias

permissions: Dispatch tasks to the hub (send_task wakes the recipient AI)
Modify hub task and session state
Read and write the git repository of the project that mounted this skill
Mint and store a node token for a manual node, and write heartbeat state files next to its config
approval_required: Dispatching and verifying are triggered by the operator's instruction; the planner stops once dispatches are sent
Running the manual-node script against a hub is an explicit operator action
